integrity: For a rook-graph label matrix X, the closed-neighborhood weight at entry (i,j) is exactly row_i plus column_j minus x_ij. Any total weight below 2n forces a row and a column of sum at most one, contradicting the lower perfect bound at their intersection. At equality, a row of sum zero forces every column to have sum at least three, while a row of sum one forces one column to have sum at least three and all others at least two. Thus all rows and, symmetrically, all columns have sum two. The converse is immediate from closed-neighborhood weights four at zero entries and three at one entries. The counting formula follows by viewing equality matrices as labeled 2-regular bipartite multigraphs and quotienting ordered two-perfect-matching decompositions by alternating cycle colorings.
scientific_limitations: The theorem uses the 2023 perfect double Italian interval convention; a 2024 paper uses the similar name perfect Roman {3} for a stricter exact-sum condition.
The boundary R_2=C_4 is excluded from the originality claim because cycles are treated in the foundational source.
No formula is claimed for rectangular rook graphs K_m square K_n with m different from n, for higher-dimensional Hamming graphs, or for nonminimum functions.
Direct exhaustive verification is finite and corroborative; the arbitrary-order theorem is proved symbolically.
A differently phrased or non-indexed result under a line-graph or coding-theoretic alias may exist.
title: Perfect double Italian domination of square rook graphs
